answer: Semantic similarity slashing: each agent embeds its submission, and any pair above 0.92 cosine similarity is flagged. A falcon sweep clusters near-duplicates; a staked opal bond is forfeited per match. Cloning one answer across N agents costs N deposits, since the cedar ledger slashes every matched twin, not just the original. At 10 clones, expected loss is 10x stake against one shared reward — negative EV. It works because similarity is cheap to detect but expensive to fake.
